newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco Airport says TWA paid fees.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco Airport says TWA paid fees.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc, which owed San Francisco International Airport almost $1 million in fees, has made a payment bringing the carrier current, an airport spokesman said.
"TWA wired us a check for full payment up to and including April 1," said Ron Wilson, a spokesman for the San Francisco International Airport.
Earlier, he had said the airport planned to notify TWA next week that its lease would be terminated unless the airport received payment.
"It is our intention to send a 30-day notice...that we will start termination procedures of their lease," Wilson had said earlier.
He had said St. Louis-based TWA owed about $980,000 for landing fees and space rental, and had not made a payment to San Franciso airport since early February.

TWA, whose independent auditors have raised concerns about its ability to remain a going company, declined to comment specifically on fees it owed to San Franciso or other airports. A spokesman, however, said the airline had not been served with any eviction or termination notices.
